title: Prefix-aware caching: hit-rate modeling, adaptive TTLs, and safe rollout flows
creator: Ava Park
description:
Problem: Prefix/key shaping and TTL policy tuning are currently manual and siloed. Teams see large cost variance across tenants because cache keys are inconsistently defined and TTLs are overprovisioned. We need an automated recommendation system plus safe apply/rollback flows so ops can reduce token cost without risking correctness or latency regressions.

Goals: reduce per-token cost by 10-25% on cacheable workloads while keeping tail latency within SLOs and avoiding correctness regressions. Deliver a playbook + automation components that produce recommended prefix groupings, TTL suggestions, and a safe apply flow (shadow simulation, canary, auto-rollback).

Scope and approach:
1) Hit-rate modeling engine: offline simulator that consumes request traces and builds a statistical model of prefix reuse and temporal locality. Uses a sliding-window estimator and exponential decay to project hit-rate for candidate prefix groupings. Key outputs: predicted hit-rate curve vs TTL, per-prefix QPS distribution, and expected cost delta.
2) Prefix grouping heuristics: propose a small set of deterministic grouping strategies (exact-key, path-prefix, producer-scoped, user-scoped, hashed-buckets) + a stochastic grouping stage that recommends merging low-traffic prefixes for training. Include rules for reserved prefixes and collision avoidance.
3) Adaptive TTL recommendations: compute TTL bands per prefix group using cost-weighted objective: maximize (saved_tokens_per_time) - lambda * (expected_miss_penalty_in_ms). Allow constraint on max allowed increase in tail P95 latency. Produce suggestions like TTL=8s for hot prefixes, TTL=120s for moderate, TTL=3600s for cold.
4) Safe apply flows: three-phase rollout: PREVIEW (simulation on historical trace), SHADOW (apply to 1% of live traffic in shadow mode and compare outputs / costs), CANARY (live apply for select routes/customers), FULL ROLLOUT with monitors and auto-rollback guardrails. Implement an automated rollback policy when cost or error metrics cross thresholds.
5) Key design guidelines: canonicalization, scope tagging, eviction-safe separators, avoiding user-identifying high-cardinality tokens in primary key, and per-tenant scoping for enterprise customers. Provide example key patterns and anti-patterns.

Telemetry and metrics: integrate with Console dashboards. Required metrics: prefix_hit_rate, prefix_qps, ttl_applied, cache_evictions, cache_misclass_rate, downstream_token_savings, apply_confidence_score. Add synthetic traffic replayer for PREVIEW and SHADOW reproducibility.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator produces reproducible hit-rate predictions within 10% of observed after shadow run.
- Automated recommendation UI produces TTL suggestions for at least 90% of high-QPS prefixes.
- Safe apply flow successfully rolls forward and auto-rolls back in a staged test cluster with injected regressions.
- Documentation and playbook published in Confluence and linked in proposal.

Deliverables:
- hitmodel-simulator binary + CI job (trace -> report)
- recommendation service API (GET /recommendations?route=...)
- rollout controller that executes PREVIEW/SHADOW/CANARY/FULL with metrics checks
- Console panel with per-prefix recommendations and simulated cost delta
- Playbook doc: key patterns, TTL bands, rollback checklist

Links and artifacts:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Prefix+Caching+Recommendations
- Design sketches (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/obfuscated/prefix-cache-ui
- Trace dataset for simulation: s3://redwood-inference-prod/traces/2026-q1-small-sample
- Example PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/auto-apply-prefix-cache

Risks and trade-offs:
- Over-aggregation of prefixes may cause correctness regressions; mitigated via shadow comparison and strict output diff thresholds.
- TTLs that are too long increase memory pressure; we will cap recommended TTLs and include eviction forecasts.
- Cost model assumptions may drift; include periodic re-evaluation and confidence scoring.

Next steps:
- Align with PM for priority and project timelines (PM: Sofia Williams).
- Build an MVP simulator and run against last 30 days of traces.
- Create Console mock showing recommendations for a single route and solicit design review.
